reasons: Shapes disagree with the smoke test in several places.
Types are not checked against live API responses.

terms.meaning: a named description of the fields an object must have
a value that must be one of a fixed list of options
a field that may be left out, marked with a question mark

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File header and purpose
sections.what: Explains that this file is the single source of shared API shapes.
sections.why: Makes the file's role clear to new readers.

sections.name: ApiResponse
sections.title: Standard success wrapper
sections.what: Describes the wrapper for successful responses: data, optional paging information, and an optional message.
sections.why: Gives every success response the same outer shape.
sections.watch_out: The smoke test reads fields at the top level, so confirm whether the API actually wraps responses this way.

sections.name: ApiError
sections.title: Standard error shape
sections.what: Describes an error response with status code, message, error name, optional field details, timestamp and path.
sections.why: Lets clients handle every error the same way.

sections.name: PaginationMeta
sections.title: Paging information
sections.what: Describes page number, page size, totals and next or previous flags.
sections.why: Lets lists show paging controls.

sections.name: PaginationQuery, UserRoleEnum, AuthProviderEnum
sections.title: Paging query and role and provider names
sections.what: Describes sorting and paging inputs, and lists the user roles and sign-in providers.
sections.why: Keeps the allowed role and provider names in one place.
sections.watch_out: The provider names here are uppercase, while the social sign-in request uses lowercase.

sections.name: RegisterRequest
sections.title: Registration request
sections.what: Describes the fields needed to create an account: email, password, full name and optional phone.
sections.why: Defines the sign-up input.

sections.name: LoginRequest
sections.title: Login request
sections.what: Describes email, password, and an optional device name and operating system.
sections.why: Lets the server record which device each session belongs to.

sections.name: SendOtpRequest
sections.title: Send code request
sections.what: Describes sending a one-time code by phone or email.
sections.why: Supports both sign-in channels.
sections.watch_out: Both fields are optional, so the rule that one must be given is not expressed here.

sections.name: VerifyOtpRequest
sections.title: Verify code request
sections.what: Describes the one-time code and the phone or email it was sent to.
sections.why: Completes the code check.
sections.watch_out: Neither field is required, so a request with neither is not ruled out by this type.

sections.name: OAuthLoginRequest
sections.title: Social sign-in request
sections.what: Describes sign-in with Google or Apple using an identity token.
sections.why: Supports third-party sign-in.
sections.watch_out: Provider names are lowercase here but uppercase in the provider list.

sections.name: BiometricRegisterRequest
sections.title: Biometric registration request
sections.what: Describes registering a device biometric key with an optional device name.
sections.why: Supports fingerprint or face sign-in.

sections.name: BiometricLoginRequest
sections.title: Biometric login request
sections.what: Describes a signature and session ID that prove the device holds the biometric key.
sections.why: Lets biometric sign-in complete without a password.

sections.name: ForgotPasswordRequest
sections.title: Forgot password request
sections.what: Describes the email address for starting a password reset.
sections.why: Starts the reset process.

sections.name: ResetPasswordRequest
sections.title: Reset password request
sections.what: Describes the reset token and the new password.
sections.why: Completes the reset process.

sections.name: ChangePasswordRequest
sections.title: Change password request
sections.what: Describes the current and new password for a signed-in user.
sections.why: Lets a user change their own password.

sections.name: AuthTokens
sections.title: Token pair
sections.what: Describes the access token, the refresh token, and how many seconds the access token lasts.
sections.why: Standard sign-in result.

sections.name: AuthResponse
sections.title: Sign-in response
sections.what: Adds the user profile and a flag saying whether the account is new, to the token pair.
sections.why: Tells the app whether to start onboarding.

sections.name: RefreshTokenRequest
sections.title: Refresh token request
sections.what: Describes the refresh token used to get a new access token.
sections.why: Keeps users signed in without asking for a password again.

sections.name: UserSession
sections.title: Signed-in session record
sections.what: Describes one signed-in device: name, operating system, IP address, last active time and creation time.
sections.why: Lets users see and end their sessions.
sections.watch_out: The IP address is personal data, so display and storage should follow privacy rules.

sections.name: RevokeSessionRequest
sections.title: End session request
sections.what: Describes the session to end.
sections.why: Supports signing a device out remotely.

sections.name: UserProfile
sections.title: User profile
sections.what: Describes a user's profile: contact details, name, birth date, gender, blood group, language, timezone and onboarding status.
sections.why: Shared shape the apps show and edit.
sections.watch_out: Date of birth and blood group are sensitive health-related data.

sections.name: UpdateProfileRequest
sections.title: Profile update request
sections.what: Describes which profile fields a user may change.
sections.why: Limits what can be edited.

sections.name: DocumentTypeEnum, ProcessingStatusEnum
sections.title: Document type and processing status names
sections.what: Lists the document categories and the states a document can be in, including withheld.
sections.why: Keeps labels identical across the system.
sections.watch_out: The smoke test uses the WITHHELD status, so it must stay in this list.

sections.name: GetUploadUrlRequest
sections.title: Request for an upload address
sections.what: Describes the file name, type, size and document type needed before an upload.
sections.why: Lets the server issue a safe upload address.
sections.watch_out: The smoke test sends no document type, but this shape requires one.

sections.name: UploadUrlResponse
sections.title: Upload address response
sections.what: Describes the upload address, the storage key and how long the address lasts.
sections.why: Gives the app what it needs to upload.

sections.name: ConfirmUploadRequest
sections.title: Confirm upload request
sections.what: Describes the storage key and document details to send once the upload finishes.
sections.why: Tells the server the file is ready to process.
sections.watch_out: The smoke test sends extra fields, such as original name and mime type, that this shape does not list.

sections.name: MedicationEntity
sections.title: Medication record
sections.what: Describes one medicine: name, dosage, timing, duration, frequency and instructions.
sections.why: Shape of a medicine read from a prescription.

sections.name: PrescriptionExtraction
sections.title: Prescription extraction result
sections.what: Describes the prescription details: doctor, clinic, diagnosis, date, medicine list, diagnosis codes and a confidence score.
sections.why: Holds the structured output from reading a prescription.
sections.watch_out: Uses underscore field names, unlike the rest of the file, which uses camel case.

sections.name: DocumentProfile
sections.title: Document summary card
sections.what: Describes a document's basic information and the status of its text reading and AI summary.
sections.why: Used in lists of documents.

sections.name: DocumentResponse
sections.title: Full document record
sections.what: Describes a document with its tags, dates, provider and doctor names, and statuses.
sections.why: Used when showing one document.
sections.watch_out: Document type here uses the fixed list, while the summary card uses plain text.

sections.name: UploadDocumentRequest
sections.title: Upload details
sections.what: Describes the details a user can give with a document, such as date, provider, doctor and tags.
sections.why: Holds the information entered during upload.

sections.name: OcrResultResponse
sections.title: Text reading result
sections.what: Describes the raw text, structured data, confidence, engine used and processing time.
sections.why: Output of the text reading step.

sections.name: AiSummaryResponse
sections.title: AI summary result
sections.what: Describes the summary text, key findings, risk flags, and the model used.
sections.why: Output of the AI summary step.

sections.name: KeyFinding
sections.title: Key finding item
sections.what: Describes one lab measurement with its value, a status from normal to critical, and a note.
sections.why: Used to highlight results to the user.

sections.name: RiskFlag
sections.title: Risk flag item
sections.what: Describes one concern with its severity and a recommendation.
sections.why: Flags results that need attention.
sections.watch_out: Severity names differ from the status names used for key findings.

sections.name: ReminderFrequencyEnum
sections.title: Reminder frequency options
sections.what: Lists how often a medicine reminder repeats, from once daily to a custom schedule.
sections.why: Gives a fixed set of choices.

sections.name: CreateMedicineReminderRequest
sections.title: Create medicine reminder request
sections.what: Describes a medicine reminder: name, dose, frequency, times, days, meal timing, start and end dates, and snooze and escalation settings.
sections.why: Input used to create a reminder.
sections.watch_out: Times of day are plain text, so their format is not enforced here.

sections.name: MedicineReminderResponse
sections.title: Medicine reminder record
sections.what: Describes a saved medicine reminder and whether it is active.
sections.why: Shape of a reminder the app displays.
sections.watch_out: Meal relation is plain text here, while the request accepts only four values.

sections.name: WaterReminderConfig
sections.title: Water reminder settings
sections.what: Describes the daily water goal, reminder interval, active hours, glass size and whether reminders are on.
sections.why: Holds the water reminder configuration.
sections.watch_out: Active hours are text, so their format is not enforced.

sections.name: WaterIntakeLog
sections.title: Water intake entry
sections.what: Describes one logged amount of water with its time.
sections.why: A single water log entry.

sections.name: WaterIntakeSummary
sections.title: Water intake summary
sections.what: Describes total intake, goal, percentage, glass count and the list of logs.
sections.why: Feeds the water summary screen.

sections.name: CreateMealReminderRequest
sections.title: Meal reminder request
sections.what: Describes a breakfast, lunch, snack or dinner reminder with its time and optional diet notes.
sections.why: Input used to create meal reminders.

sections.name: LogReminderRequest
sections.title: Reminder response request
sections.what: Describes how the user answered a reminder: taken, skipped or snoozed, with optional notes.
sections.why: Records whether the user followed the reminder.

sections.name: TimelineEntry
sections.title: Health timeline entry
sections.what: Describes one timeline item, which can be a document, a reminder log or a health record, with date, title, subtitle and extra data.
sections.why: Gives one combined list of health events.
sections.watch_out: Extra data is untyped, so its contents are not checked.

sections.name: TrendDataPoint
sections.title: Trend data point
sections.what: Describes one measured value with its date, unit and status.
sections.why: A single point on a trend chart.

sections.name: ParameterTrend
sections.title: Parameter trend
sections.what: Describes one lab measurement over time, with its unit, reference range and data points.
sections.why: Feeds trend charts.
sections.watch_out: Reference limits may be missing, so charts must handle empty values.

sections.name: AdherenceStats
sections.title: Adherence statistics
sections.what: Describes counts of reminders taken, skipped and missed for a period, plus a rate.
sections.why: Summarizes how well reminders are followed.
sections.watch_out: The rate is supplied by the server and this file does not check that it matches the counts.

sections.name: CreateFamilyGroupRequest
sections.title: Create family group request
sections.what: Describes the name of a new family group.
sections.why: Input used to create a group.

sections.name: AddFamilyMemberRequest
sections.title: Add family member request
sections.what: Describes how to add someone by phone or email, their role, relationship, and permissions to view, edit or manage reminders.
sections.why: Input used to add members.
sections.watch_out: Phone and email are both optional, so this type does not require either one.

sections.name: FamilyGroupResponse
sections.title: Family group record
sections.what: Describes a family group with its name and member list.
sections.why: Shape used to show a group.

sections.name: FamilyMemberResponse
sections.title: Family member record
sections.what: Describes one member with their role, relationship, and view, edit and reminder permissions.
sections.why: Shape used to show members and their access.

sections.name: CreateShareRequest
sections.title: Doctor share request
sections.what: Describes the doctor's details and how many days the share lasts.
sections.why: Input used to share records with a doctor.

sections.name: DoctorShareResponse
sections.title: Doctor share record
sections.what: Describes a share link with its token, URL, access level, expiry date and how many times it was opened.
sections.why: Shape used to show and track shares.
sections.watch_out: The access level is plain text, not a fixed list.

sections.name: CreateChatSessionRequest
sections.title: Start chat request
sections.what: Describes starting a chat with a context type, which can be general, a document, or a health query, and an optional related record.
sections.why: Input used to open a chat.

sections.name: SendMessageRequest
sections.title: Send chat message request
sections.what: Describes the message body sent in a chat.
sections.why: Input used to send a message.
sections.watch_out: This type names the field content, but the smoke test sends message, so one of them is wrong.

sections.name: ChatMessageResponse
sections.title: Chat message record
sections.what: Describes a chat message with its sender role, text, extra data and time.
sections.why: Shape of messages shown in a chat.

sections.name: RegisterDeviceRequest
sections.title: Device registration request
sections.what: Describes registering a device for push notifications, with a token for Android or Apple and the platform.
sections.why: Lets the server send alerts to the device.
sections.watch_out: Push tokens identify a device and should be handled with care.

sections.name: NotificationResponse
sections.title: Notification record
sections.what: Describes one notification: type, channel, title, body, extra data, status, read time and creation time.
sections.why: Shape of notifications shown in the app.

summary: One file holding the shared data shapes for requests and responses, covering sign-in, documents, reminders, family, doctor sharing, chat and notifications.
purpose: Defines the contract between the API and the apps so both sides use the same field names.
why: Likely reason: one source of truth prevents the backend and frontend from disagreeing about fields.
how: Written as TypeScript interfaces and union types, grouped by feature. Other code imports them to type its requests and responses.
inputs: No run-time inputs. The types are used when the code is compiled.
outputs: Type definitions only. No code runs from this file.
risks: Types are checked only during compilation, not against live data. Several shapes disagree with the smoke test or with each other: the confirm-upload fields, the chat message field name, and the upload-URL requirements. Naming styles are mixed; the prescription extraction uses underscores.
debug: If a request is rejected, compare the field names here with what the caller sends. Run typecheck to find code that uses the wrong shape.
